It typically results in an irregularly irregular pulse and can cause symptoms such as palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. On an ECG, AFib shows a chaotic pattern with no discernible P waves and a rapid ventricular response.Atrial flutter (AFlt), on the other hand, involves a more organized but still abnormal electrical rhythm originating in the atria. It usually presents with a regular but rapid heartbeat and can be recognized on an ECG by a sawtooth pattern known as the F wave. AFlt often leads to a regular ventricular response, which can be either normal or rapid, depending on the conduction through the AV node.In summary, while both conditions involve abnormal atrial rhythms, AFib is more chaotic and irregular, whereas AFlt has a more organized but still abnormal pattern.
